origin: cwe/434 Key Principles: verify the file's actual content rather than the filename extension or client-supplied Content-Type header

finding.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
finding.summary: upload_avatar stores the object with ContentType set directly from the client-supplied content_type parameter, with no check against the actual file bytes. A caller can pass ContentType=text/html (or any type unrelated to file_bytes), and the object is later served - via a presigned URL or public bucket policy - with that attacker-chosen Content-Type, so a browser renders it as HTML instead of downloading it as an opaque file, executing any embedded script.

trap: Validating content_type against an allowlist of image MIME types before the put_object call closes the finding only if the check is against the real content: content_type is still the client-supplied header, unrelated to what file_bytes actually contains, so a request can pass image/png in the header while file_bytes is HTML with a script payload - the object is still served back with the client's claimed, unverified Content-Type. The check has to detect the type from file_bytes itself (a content-sniffing library, not the parameter) and pass the detected type - never content_type - to ContentType, in addition to setting ContentDisposition to attachment and, where the object type allows it, re-encoding the bytes before upload.
must_preserve: upload_avatar still stores valid image uploads and they remain retrievable with a correct image Content-Type. An upload whose actual bytes do not match an allowed image type is rejected before put_object runs, or is stored with a Content-Type that reflects its real detected type, never the caller-supplied value.
